result.title: SmoothShift: Disrupting Visual Adversarial Attacks on LVLMs at Test Time
result.summary: Visual adversarial perturbations can substantially impair large vision-language models (LVLMs) despite introducing only subtle input changes. To understand how these small changes cause substantial errors, we investigate their optimization and propagation through the model, revealing two key findings. First, stronger attacks rely on finer iterative optimization, while subtle input perturbations induce representation discrepancies that are amplified layer by layer through the vision encoder and persist in the language model. Second, disrupting the alignment between within-patch input patterns and the model's computation reduces clean-adversarial representation discrepancies and substantially weakens attacks. Together, these findings suggest that adversarial effectiveness depends on both fine-grained perturbation patterns and their coupling with the model's computation. Motivated by these findings, we propose SmoothShift, a lightweight, training-free defense that combines local smoothing and spatial transformations. Smoothing weakens fine-grained perturbation patterns, while spatial transformations disrupt their alignment with the encoder's patch grid. SmoothShift requires no model updates, auxiliary networks, or additional model inference. Experiments cover three LVLM families on four datasets and robustly fine-tuned Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training (CLIP) models on eight classification datasets. Evaluations across eight attack methods and multiple perturbation budgets demonstrate improved robustness while largely preserving clean performance. SmoothShift also provides robustness gains under defense-aware attacks using mixed-gradient BPDA with EOT.

AI.brief_summary: 论文分析视觉对抗扰动在 LVLM 中的优化与传播，发现细微扰动引起的表示差异会经视觉编码器逐层放大并持续到语言模型，且扰动的有效性还依赖其与 patch 网格计算的耦合；据此提出免训练的 SmoothShift 防御，用局部平滑与空间变换削弱细粒度扰动模式。
AI.relevance_reason: 其对「表示差异逐层放大」与「输入模式—计算对齐」的诊断，可能为核查 LVR 中视觉细节是否被内部状态忠实保留、以及位置/结构敏感性提供问题表述，但该文面向分类鲁棒性而非推理，联系仍是概念性的。
